chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking Zurarah, saying: 'Did you perform the Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And did you become weak/tired?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I have become strong.' He said: 'If you fear weakness, then ride, for it is stronger for you in supplication.'

key_terms.السَّعْي: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on riding during Sa'i if one is weak?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Zurarah that while walking is the normative practice for Sa'i, riding is permitted if physical weakness might hinder the quality of one's supplication. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of *rukub* (riding) being a valid alternative to ensure the devotee remains energetic for *dua*, emphasizing that the spiritual benefit of the ritual is tied to the worshipper's physical capacity to engage in devotion.
